existing_rows_audit.detail: Balyasny has no Paris office. The firm's own locations page (https://www.bamfunds.com/about-us/locations) lists Aalborg, Abu Dhabi, Austin, Boston, Chicago, Copenhagen, Dubai, Greenwich, Hong Kong, Houston, London, Miami, New York, San Francisco, Santa Monica, Singapore, Tokyo, Toronto and Warsaw - no Paris. The live careers portal's own location filter (https://bambusdev.my.site.com/s/) offers Austin, Chicago, Dubai, Geneva, Greenwich, Hong Kong, Houston, Japan, London, New York, Singapore, Stamford, Tokyo, Warsaw - again no Paris, and zero of the 128 open reqs is in France. This row should be deleted; Warsaw is BAM's actual EU engineering hub and is where the EU C++ seat lives.

The London office is confirmed (23 King St, London UK, per the careers portal's own office record) and C++ seats are genuinely open there, but nothing is posted under the title 'Quantitative Developer' in London. The two actual C++ development reqs are 'Junior C++ Developer' (REQ8337, https://bambusdev.my.site.com/s/details?jobReq=Junior-C-plus-plus-Developer_REQ8337) and 'Senior Low Latency C++ Developer' (REQ8336). The row's stated requirements (modern C++, Linux/networking/CPU-memory performance, BS/MS, no finance background required) do match REQ8337 well. The 'Eligibility Gate: 0-3 YoE typical' claim is also broadly right for REQ8337, which states no minimum experience. The comp figure of GBP 110-170k was not verifiable - the only figure BAM publishes on REQ8337 is a USD 150-200k base range, which is a US pay-transparency disclosure on a multi-city req, not a London number.

notes:
Method: BAM's careers portal is a Salesforce Experience Cloud site (https://bambusdev.my.site.com/s/) that renders nothing without JavaScript, so plain fetching returns a CSS error page. I drove it with a headless browser and then read its own Apex data services (BamJobRequisitionInfoDataService.searchJobRequisitions, rolePage.getJobByJobReqTitleURL / getLocation / getDescription) to enumerate all 128 open reqs and pull each posting's real location set and full description. Every role above was read from the firm's own posting - all verified-primary. Direct req URLs follow the pattern https://bambusdev.my.site.com/s/details?jobReq=<slug>_<REQ number>; they are client-side routed, so they need a normal browser to render.

Important data caveat: the list endpoint's location field is unreliable (it showed REQ8336 as New York only, while the posting itself says Chicago/London/New York). All locations above come from the per-req getLocation call, which matches what the posting displays.

In-scope office confirmation: London, Warsaw, Singapore, Hong Kong and Tokyo all appear both on the firm's locations page and as live req locations. 'Japan' also appears as a separate portal location value (used by REQ7610 Japan L/S Analyst - Tokyo), which is Tokyo. Geneva appears as a portal location on REQ8259 (an oil analyst seat advertised as 'Geneva or Zug', Switzerland) even though Geneva is not on the public locations page - Switzerland is outside the brief's EU/UK/SG/HK/Shanghai/Tokyo scope and the role is a fundamental commodities analyst seat, so it was excluded; flag it if Swiss seats are wanted, since the candidate holds a CH permit. Shanghai: BAM has no mainland China office.

Deliberate exclusions worth knowing about: (1) Hong Kong 'Quantitative Researcher (Summer Internship)' REQ8057 and '(Off Cycle Internship)' REQ8058 are student-gated - 'Full time for 2027 summer & part-time off cycle for 2026 Sep-Dec' - and out of scope for a working professional. (2) The Warsaw and Hong Kong 'Engineer, Execution Technology' reqs (REQ8374, REQ8371, REQ8326) sound like low-latency C++ but the qualifications explicitly say Java (5+ years, or 10-15+ for the senior Warsaw one) with C# maintenance, so they are not C++ seats. (3) 'Engineer - Multi-Asset Arbitrage Technology' REQ8079 (London/NY) is a React front-end role despite the title. (4) 'Macro AI Engineering Lead' REQ7951 was excluded as a people-management role. (5) Numerous Warsaw reqs (SRE, network, QA, UI/UX, front-end, data ops, Python data platform) fall outside the four tracks.

Compensation: every figure quoted is a base-salary range BAM itself publishes on the req (Base_Compensation_Low/High, USD, annually). These are US pay-transparency disclosures attached to multi-city reqs - treat them as an indication of level, not as a London, Warsaw, Singapore, Hong Kong or Tokyo offer. Reqs that are single-location outside the US carry no published figure, and I have left comp_local empty rather than extrapolate.

Coverage gap: BAM shows 'Posted N Days Ago' but no explicit expiry. Several rows above are 100-210 days old (REQ7211 at 211 days, REQ7949/7950 at 166, REQ6905 at 138, REQ8042 at 137). They are still served as open by the portal, but staleness is a real risk on those.
